title: GLEE: A Unified Framework and Benchmark for Language-based Economic Environments
why: Cited in paper.md Step 6 / paper_draft as a second controlled dataset substrate (parameterized two-player sequential language-based economic games) to test whether magnitude/cross-model findings are stable beyond the fully synthetic controller-generated scenarios; a structural exemplar for standardized LLM economic-game benchmarking, not a method-twin (no injected tactic, no concealed-valuation surplus-transfer statistic).

title: Decoupling Strategy and Generation in Negotiation Dialogues
why: Source of the CraigslistBargain naturalistic price-negotiation dialogue dataset, cited in paper.md Step 6 / paper_draft Experimental Setup as an external-validity substrate to test whether tactic-injection findings generalize beyond experimenter-authored scenario phrasing to real negotiation language; a dataset source, not a method-twin.

title: Deal or No Deal? End-to-End Learning for Negotiation Dialogues
why: Source of the Deal-or-No-Deal multi-issue human-human negotiation dialogue dataset, cited in paper.md Step 6 / paper_draft Experimental Setup as a second naturalistic corpus for the external-validity check alongside CraigslistBargain; a dataset source, not a method-twin.

title: TERMS-Bench: Diagnosing LLM Negotiation Agents Beyond Deal Rate
why: Environment-as-verifier bilateral negotiation benchmark: counterpart latent type/policy/payoff concealed from the agent, visible to the evaluator; continuous surplus-extraction diagnostics for 13 LLM agents. Occupies the concealed-payoff mechanical-surplus-scoring apparatus this draft previously claimed implicitly; injects no manipulation treatment, so B5.1's per-tactic causal estimand remains the delta. Surfaced by the 2026-08 review pass; cited as termsbench2026.

title: How Does Cognitive Bias Affect Large Language Models? A Case Study on the Anchoring Effect in Price Negotiation Simulations
why: Instructs a seller LLM to apply the anchoring effect in price-negotiation simulations and measures the final-deal-price shift with anchor level -- the single nearest prior measurement to RQ2 for one of the four tactics. No assertiveness-matched control, no two-sided concealed-and-verified reservation, no surplus-share statistic, no cross-tactic catalog. Surfaced by the 2026-08 review pass; cited as anchoringbias2025.

title: EvoEmo: Towards Evolved Emotional Policies for Adversarial LLM Agents in Multi-Turn Price Negotiation
why: Population-based genetic optimization of emotional policies for adversarial LLM buyers in multi-turn price negotiation, scored by success rate, efficiency, and buyer savings. Prices an optimized adversarial policy, not a fixed named tactic isolated causally; overlaps B5.1's emotional-pressure tactic on the outcome side only. Surfaced by the 2026-08 review pass; cited as evoemo2025.

title: When LLM Agents Negotiate: Private Information and Dynamic Bargaining in Supply Chains
why: Nine LLMs in autonomous supply-chain procurement negotiation under private information, scored against game-theoretic benchmarks; surplus division decomposed by provider and prompt configuration (prompt config ~90% of explained variance). Continuous surplus measurement with no injected tactic treatment; decay-context neighbor for the continuous-economic-quantity framing. Surfaced by the 2026-08 review pass; cited as supplychain2026.
